[1/5] repair fixed_duties fields, whitelist cfg_language, tell the user when a state file was set aside and let them download it; [2/5] keep only the 5 newest quarantined copies per file; [3/5] change-password form plus a prompt for legacy hashes kept for long passwords; [4/5] faster tests by lowering bcrypt cost inside tests only; [5/5] scrub the home path from unpushed local history, record a project guideline, push without force

impact_assessment.why: The review found two normalizer gaps that crash Generate or the page, a silent quarantine that looks like data loss, unbounded quarantine files, legacy long-password hashes with no way to change them, slow tests, and a Windows home path in 23 tracked lines that a push would publish
impact_assessment.benefits: No crash from odd saved values, the user is told what happened to their data, bounded disk use, a way off the weak hash, a faster suite, and no home path published
impact_assessment.risks: contract: load_db returns more than before and a new password-change path writes the users store; dependency: none; concurrency: password change rewrites one users entry via replace_json_entry as in ADR-017; state: history rewrite changes the SHAs of unpushed commits that reforge.json references
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests per milestone, project check before each commit, a backup branch before the rewrite and a restore path, reforge status verified after the rewrite, push never forced
